##two subsets going by ratings that shows which drug reviews-
##got high ratings ( >7) and low ratings ( <7)
df_high = drugsdf[drugsdf['rating'] > 7]
df_low = drugsdf[drugsdf['rating'] < 7]
##for topic modeling creating two subsets of usefulcount to show how users found the review, if a lot of users found the reviews helpful or less found the review helpful.
##This shows how much users the reviews were able to reach
df_moreusefl = drugsdf[drugsdf['usefulCount'] > 50]
df_lessusefl = drugsdf[drugsdf['usefulCount'] <= 50]
from bertopic import BERTopic
import plotly
##Topic model for each subset: high rating
topic_model_high = BERTopic(verbose=True)
topics_high, probs_high = topic_model_high.fit_transform(df_high['review'])

##Topic model for each subset: low rating
topic_model_low = BERTopic(verbose=True)
topics_low, probs_low = topic_model_low.fit_transform(df_low['review'])

##Topic model for each subset: more usefulCount
topic_model_moreusef = BERTopic(verbose=True)
topics_moreusef, probs_moreusef = topic_model_moreusef.fit_transform(df_moreusefl['review'])

##Topic model for each subset: less useful
topic_model_lessusef = BERTopic(verbose=True)
topics_lessusef, probs_lessusef = topic_model_lessusef.fit_transform(df_lessusefl['review'])

Describe the analysis you did and why you made the analytic choices you did.

In this analysis, we used Topic Modeling to higlight the topics within the dataset to uncover themes and patterns of topics revolving around patients' drug reviews. We did segmentation of the dataset by Rating and UsefulCounts.

Separating the reviews based on ratings and usefulness allowed for more nuanced insights. Users with high ratings likely experienced different outcomes than those with low ratings, and reviews deemed "more useful" could reflect richer, more detailed experiences. These distinctions help in identifying variations in themes across different subsets of data.

BERTopic was chosen for its ability to use transformer-based embeddings, which provide a more advanced and contextual richness than traditional topic modeling techniques (such as LDA). This method is efficient at identifying nuanced patterns within textual data.

High rating

  • This has 4 clusters which revolve around themes/patterns regarding reproductive health, digestive or gut concerns, mental health struggles and skin issues. Most users seem to give a high rating to reviews which hold these themes. This analysis through BERTopic helped uncover the core experiences that users associate with high ratings, such as mental and reproductive health improvements.

Low rating

  • 3 clusters are included with the low ratings topics, and they mostly revolve around patterns highlighting reproductive health, digestive concerns, and allergies.

More usefulCount

  • There are no clusters, but individual patterns. The lack of clusters and fewer topics suggest that the content of highly useful reviews is more coherent and focused around specific themes. This coherence could indicate that these reviews provide in-depth and focused feedback, which may address a consistent set of issues, such as drug efficacy, precise outcomes, and detailed personal experiences. These kinds of reviews may be more actionable or informative to others, resulting in higher usefulness ratings.

Less usefulCount

  • ⁠The existence of multiple clusters and more fragmented topics in the less useful reviews suggests greater variability in content. These reviews might be less focused, addressing a wider array of topics without going into sufficient detail. This could include general remarks, vague experiences, or superficial commentary, which might reduce their usefulness to readers

Overall, the main topics are those which trend in reproductive, digestive, and mental health concerns when it comes to drug efficacy or effectiveness. The decision to segment the dataset based on rating and usefulness, along with the clustering insights from the intertopic distance map, allowed for a deeper understanding of what drives positive user reviews. Clusters represent related topics that share overlapping themes.

The lack of clusters and fewer topics suggest that the content of highly useful reviews is more coherent and focused around specific themes. This coherence could indicate that these reviews provide in-depth and focused feedback, which may address a consistent set of issues, such as drug efficacy, precise outcomes, and detailed personal experiences. These kinds of reviews may be more actionable or informative to others, resulting in higher usefulness ratings.
